config.title: Query Building in RTK

intro.title: RTK Query: Writing Your First builder.query
intro.body: In this lesson you will construct a complete RTK Query endpoint from scratch, one surgical micro-step at a time. You will understand every token in the expression `getPosts: builder.query<Post[], void>({ query: () => '/posts' })` — what it does, why it exists, and how to recall it from memory without looking anything up. You begin by defining the data shape with a TypeScript interface, then move into the RTK Query API configuration layer, and finish by wiring the complete endpoint and exported hook.
intro.usecase: RTK Query is the data-fetching and caching layer built into Redux Toolkit. In real applications it replaces dozens of lines of manual action creators, reducers, selectors, and loading-state boilerplate with a single declarative endpoint definition. You will use `builder.query` every time your UI needs to READ data from a server — fetching lists, profiles, catalogues, and more. Mastering this pattern is the gateway to auto-generated React hooks like `useGetPostsQuery()` that handle loading, error, and data states with minimal extra code.

objectives: Build a query with dynamic parameters by typing the endpoint arg as an object (e.g. { page: number; filter: string }) and constructing the URL with template literals so multiple typed pieces work together as one coherent UI pattern.

Use the transformResponse option typed as (raw: RawResponse) => TransformedType to normalize API data before it hits the cache so the pattern drives visible behavior and can be verified in the UI, runtime, or compiler.

Apply the providesTags option typed as (result, error, arg) => TagDescription<TagType>[] to associate cache tags with a query result so the learner sees how a typed pattern changes behavior, reuse, or safety in practice.

Apply the invalidatesTags option on a mutation to automatically refetch all queries that provide the invalidated tag so the learner sees how a typed pattern changes behavior, reuse, or safety in practice so async data is handled with an explicit and safe data shape.

steps.title: Define the Post TypeScript Interface
steps.instruction: Before RTK Query can know what shape of data to expect back from the server, you must tell TypeScript. In **api.ts**, write an `interface` named `Post` with three fields: `id` (number), `title` (string), and `body` (string).
steps.hint: Use the `interface` keyword followed by the name. Each field sits on its own line ending with a semicolon.
steps.expectedOutcome: An `interface Post` exists with id: number, title: string, and body: string. This interface will be used as the result type in `builder.query` later.
successCriteria: Fields id, title, and body use the correct types
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! TypeScript now knows what a Post looks like. You will plug `Post[]` into the generic in a later step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Check that id, title, and body are all present with types number, string, string.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use: `interface Post { id: number; title: string; body: string; }`

steps.title: Import createApi and fetchBaseQuery
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, at the top of the file, add an import that brings in **`createApi`** and **`fetchBaseQuery`** from **`'@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'`**.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement with both names in curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Imports ready. Next you will open the `createApi` options object.
steps.feedbackPartial: Check spelling and ensure both helpers come from `@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react`.

steps.title: Open createApi and set reducerPath
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, below the `Post` interface, declare **`const postsApi`** assigned to **`createApi({ ... })`**. Inside the options object, add **`reducerPath: 'postsApi'`**.
steps.hint: `reducerPath` registers this API slice in the Redux store under that key.
steps.feedbackCorrect: `reducerPath` is set. Next you will wire `fetchBaseQuery` as `baseQuery`.
steps.feedbackPartial: Ensure `reducerPath` lives inside the object passed to `createApi`.
steps.feedbackWrong: Declare `const postsApi = createApi({ reducerPath: 'postsApi' });` (you may add `baseQuery` in the same object if you already know the next step).

steps.title: Add baseQuery with fetchBaseQuery
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, inside the **same** `createApi` options object as `reducerPath`, add **`baseQuery`** set to **`fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com' })`**. Do **not** add **`endpoints`** yet — you will add it in the next step.
steps.hint: `baseQuery` tells RTK Query how to reach the network; `fetchBaseQuery` is the usual HTTP adapter.
steps.expectedOutcome: `baseQuery` uses `fetchBaseQuery` with the JSONPlaceholder base URL. The `createApi` call still has no `endpoints` property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Network wiring is in place. Next you will add the `endpoints` factory.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add `baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com' })` inside the options object.

steps.title: Add the endpoints Factory Function
steps.instruction: Inside `createApi({})` in **api.ts**, add `endpoints: (builder) => ({})` — a function that receives `builder` and returns an empty object for now.
steps.hint: Return an object literal with `({})` so the `{` is not parsed as a block body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: `builder` is now in scope for the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use an arrow function that returns `({})`.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add exactly: `endpoints: (builder) => ({})` inside the createApi options.

steps.title: Start the getPosts endpoint with builder.query
steps.instruction: Inside the object returned by `endpoints`, object literals need a key and value. In **api.ts**, add **`getPosts:`** with the value starting as just **`builder.query`** (no generics or call yet). So far: `getPosts: builder.query`. The name `getPosts` is what RTK Query uses to generate `useGetPostsQuery`.
steps.hint: `builder.query` is the read-data tool; `builder.mutation` is for writes.
steps.expectedOutcome: `getPosts: builder.query` appears inside the endpoints object.
successCriteria: `builder.query` is the start of the value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Right tool and name. Next you will add generics.
steps.feedbackPartial: You need both a property name (`getPosts`) and `builder.query` as the value.

steps.title: Complete builder.query generics: Post[], void
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, after `builder.query`, write the full generic **`builder.query<Post[], void>`**: open `<` right after `query`, add the result type **`Post[]`** (the `/posts` response is a list of posts), then a comma, then **`void`** as the argument type — this query takes no runtime parameters — and close with `>`.
steps.hint: Pattern: `<ResultType, ArgType>`. List responses use `Post[]`. When there is nothing to pass into the hook at runtime, the second type is `void`.
steps.expectedOutcome: `getPosts: builder.query<Post[], void>` is present with both type parameters and the generic closed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Signature complete: many posts out, nothing in — you are ready to open the config object next.
steps.feedbackPartial: Use `builder.query<Post[], void>` — comma between `Post[]` and `void`, then `>`.

steps.title: Open the configuration object with a function call
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, **call** `builder.query<Post[], void>` with an open config object: **`({`** — so the line ends with `builder.query<Post[], void>({`.
steps.hint: Parenthesis `(` starts the call; `{` starts the config object.
steps.expectedOutcome: `builder.query<Post[], void>({` is written; config object is open.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Config object opened. Next: the required `query` field.
steps.feedbackPartial: After `void>` add `({` to call and open the config.

steps.title: Write the query property key
steps.instruction: Inside the config object in **api.ts**, add the key **`query:`** (RTK Query reads this to build the request).
steps.hint: Only the key and colon this step; the arrow function comes next.
successCriteria: The property name is `query` followed by a colon
steps.feedbackCorrect: Required field named. Next: the function value.

steps.title: Add the empty parameter list for query
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, after `query:`, add the start of an arrow function with an **empty** parameter list: **`()`** (ArgType was `void`).

steps.title: Add the fat arrow =>
steps.feedbackCorrect: Almost there — return the path string next.

steps.title: Return the path '/posts'
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, after `=>`, return the path string **`'/posts'`** so the full line is **`query: () => '/posts'`**. RTK Query joins this with your `baseUrl`.
steps.hint: Relative path only; `baseUrl` already includes the host.

steps.title: Close the config object and the builder.query call
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, close the config with **`}`** and the call with **`)`** so the endpoint value ends with **`})`** after the query line.
steps.expectedOutcome: `getPosts: builder.query<Post[], void>({ query: () => '/posts' })` is syntactically complete.
successCriteria: Config and call are closed with `})`
steps.feedbackCorrect: Endpoint expression is valid. Next: export the hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: After `'/posts'` add `})` to close object and call.
steps.feedbackWrong: End with `query: () => '/posts' })` on the getPosts property.

steps.title: Export useGetPostsQuery
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, after the `createApi` call, export the generated hook: **`export const { useGetPostsQuery } = postsApi;`** (use the same API const name you used for `createApi`).
steps.hint: Hook name is derived from the endpoint key `getPosts`.
steps.expectedOutcome: `useGetPostsQuery` is exported from the same object as `createApi`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: You can now import `useGetPostsQuery` in components (with store setup elsewhere).
steps.feedbackPartial: Destructure `useGetPostsQuery` from your exported API object.

steps.title: Recall: full api module from memory
steps.instruction: In **api.ts**, rewrite the entire module from memory: import, `Post` interface, `postsApi` with `getPosts`, and **`export const { useGetPostsQuery } = postsApi;`**. This step checks recall of the full pattern.
steps.hint: Order: import → interface → createApi → export hooks.
